title: Remimazolam attenuates myocardial ischemia-reperfusion injury by inhibiting the NF-kB pathway of macrophage inflammation.
authors: Xu, Hao; Chen, Yizhu; Xie, Pengyun; Lei, Tailong; Liu, Keyu; Liu, Xiaolei; Tang, Jin; Zhang, Liangqing; Yang, Jihong; Hu, Zhe
one_liner_zh: 该文研究瑞马唑仑通过抑制NF-kB通路减轻心肌缺血再灌注损伤，虽涉及分子对接但对象为药物-蛋白，非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或MD方法，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Inflammation is a major contributing factor in myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury, and targeting macrophage inflammation is an effective strategy for myocardial I/R therapy. Though remimazolam is approved for sedation, induction, and the maintenance of general anesthesia in cardiac surgery, its effect on cardiac function during the perioperative period has not been reported. Therefore, this research aimed to explore the impact of remimazolam on inflammation during myocardial ischemia/reperfusion (I/R) injury. METHODS: An in vivo myocardial I/R mice model and an in vitro macrophage inflammation model were used to confirm remimazolam's cardiac protective effect. In vivo, we used echocardiography, hematoxylin and eosin (HE), and terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase dUTP nick end labeling (TUNEL) staining to determine remimazolam's therapeutic effects on myocardial I/R injury and inflammation. In vitro, we employed enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), Western blot, Real-time Quantitative PCR (qPCR), flow cytometry, and immunofluorescence staining to assess inflammatory responses, especially remimazolam's effects on macrophage polarization after I/R. Furthermore, molecular docking was used to identify its potential binding targets on the inflammatory pathway to explore the mechanism of remimazolam. RESULTS: Remimazolam exhibited significant anti-myocardial I/R injury activity by inhibiting macrophage-mediated inflammation to reduce myocardial infarction, enhancing cardiac function. In addition, macrophage depletion counteracted improved cardiac function by remimazolam treatment. Mechanistically, the activated NF-kB signaling pathway and phosphorylation of p50 and p65 were repressed for anti-inflammatory effect. Consistently, two binding sites on p50 and p65 were identified by molecular docking to affect their phosphorylation of the Ser, Arg, Asp, and His residues, thus regulating NF-kappaB pathway activity. CONCLUSION: Our results unveil the therapeutic potential of remimazolam against myocardial I/R injury by inhibiting macrophages polarizing into the M1 type, alleviating inflammation.
abstract_zh: 背景：炎症是心肌缺血/再灌注（I/R）损伤的主要促成因素，靶向巨噬细胞炎症是心肌I/R治疗的有效策略。尽管瑞马唑仑已被批准用于心脏手术中的镇静、诱导及全身麻醉维持，但其在围手术期对心脏功能的影响尚未见报道。因此，本研究旨在探讨瑞马唑仑在心肌缺血/再灌注（I/R）损伤期间对炎症的影响。方法：采用体内心肌I/R小鼠模型和体外巨噬细胞炎症模型，以确认瑞马唑仑的心脏保护作用。在体内实验中，我们使用超声心动图、苏木精-伊红（HE）染色和末端脱氧核苷酸转移酶dUTP缺口末端标记（TUNEL）染色，以确定瑞马唑仑对心肌I/R损伤及炎症的治疗效果。在体外实验中，我们采用酶联免疫吸附测定（ELISA）、Western blot、实时定量PCR（qPCR）、流式细胞术和免疫荧光染色，评估炎症反应，特别是瑞马唑仑对I/R后巨噬细胞极化的影响。此外，利用分子对接技术识别其在炎症通路上的潜在结合靶点，以探索瑞马唑仑的作用机制。结果：瑞马唑仑通过抑制巨噬细胞介导的炎症，减少心肌梗死面积并增强心脏功能，表现出显著的心肌I/R损伤拮抗活性。此外，巨噬细胞耗竭抵消了瑞马唑仑治疗改善的心脏功能。机制上，激活的NF-kB信号通路及p50和p65的磷酸化受到抑制，从而发挥抗炎作用。一致地，分子对接识别出p50和p65上的两个结合位点，影响其Ser、Arg、Asp和His残基的磷酸化，进而调节NF-kappaB通路活性。结论：我们的结果揭示了瑞马唑仑通过抑制巨噬细胞向M1型极化、减轻炎症，对心肌I/R损伤的治疗潜力。
